summary: Duplicate gateway route metric on multi-homed laptops causes asymmetric paths and intermittent failures to internal k8s APIs
description: Issue summary: Multiple employees on macOS laptops that are docked (USB-C dock providing wired Ethernet) are observing intermittent failures when calling internal Kubernetes-backed APIs (gRPC timeouts and 502s from the auth-proxy). Impact: Broad internal impact for office-based employees using the docked wired interface; affects engineers and support staff. Suspected root cause: laptops are receiving a duplicate default gateway via DHCP on both the VPN interface and the dock Ethernet with conflicting route metrics, producing asymmetric paths to our k8s cluster nodes which drop TCP connections from unexpected return paths. Timing: Started 2026-03-10 09:20 PST after a DHCP lease policy change rolled to the branch site DHCP server.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect MacBook to office Wi-Fi + WireGuard VPN and confirm normal behaviour
2) Plug USB-C dock with wired Ethernet (DHCP) into laptop while VPN is active
3) Run: ipconfig getifaddr en0; netstat -rn; scutil --dns to inspect route/gateway configuration
4) Attempt to curl internal-config-api (gRPC) or open /internal/dashboard and observe intermittent 502s / timeouts
5) Run tcpdump on laptop (udp/tcp) and on k8s node to observe SYN from one interface and SYN-ACK returning to a different interface.
6) Reproducible when dock Ethernet and VPN both advertise default route with equal metric and asymmetric return traffic occurs.
observed_behavior: gRPC connections to internal-config-api either timeout after retries or return immediate connection resets. Traceroute from laptop shows outbound packets going via VPN tunnel but return packets to k8s node reach the office gateway then back to the dock interface, causing stateful firewall on the node/edge to drop the connection. Intermittent: 30-70% of requests fail under load.
expected_behavior: Packets for established sessions should follow symmetric paths so that TCP state is preserved. When VPN is active, return traffic for internal API connections should flow through the same interface and tunnel the request was sent on, preserving connection state and preventing firewall drops.
logs: laptop tcpdump snippet: SYN src 10.66.12.34:54328 -> 10.10.5.12:443; SYN-ACK src 10.10.5.12:443 -> 10.66.12.34:54328 received on different local IP
k8s node iptables: conntrack shows ESTABLISHED entries with mismatched src/dst pair causing resets
vpn logs (wireguard): peer shows inbound packet but no corresponding conntrack entry on node side
dhcp server lease change log (branch-dhcp-02): 2026-03-10T09:15:21 - rolled new default-gateway metric option to ethernet scope
investigation_notes: 09:35 - Collected netstat -rn from affected host: two default routes present, one via wg0 (10.66.0.1) and one via en3 (192.168.50.1) with identical precedence metric -> kernel chooses based on interface ordering, causing flips.

10:00 - Confirmed DHCP change on branch DHCP cluster rolled a new option that made wired interface advertise default-gateway and metric 0 (previously metric 100), resulting in identical metrics across interfaces.
10:30 - Reproduced locally: ip route show table main demonstrates alternating next-hop based on interface binding, traceroute confirms asymmetric return path.
11:05 - Hypothesis: stateful firewall rules / conntrack at k8s node validate reverse path; unexpected return source IP causes connection reset. This matches observed SYN/SYN-ACK mismatch in tcpdump.
11:45 - Temporary mitigation tested: manually set 'service order' (networksetup -ordernetworkservices) and adjust interface metrics on macOS using route change; immediate improvement for repro cases.
12:15 - SRE confirmed similar symptoms on linux laptops when connected to USB-ethernet dock; problem not macOS-specific but OS networking stack differences change flakiness.
12:50 - Escalated to Networking team; linked DHCP change request id DHCP-2026-0310 (internal ticket) as likely root cause.
comments: Sofia Martinez (reporter) 2026-03-10 09:30: Logged initial report after two engineers raised tickets in #infra. Provided pcap and netstat output.
Liam O'Connor (assignee) 2026-03-10 10:05: Starting triage. Reproduced on my docked MBP. Marking P1 due to broad office impact.

Network Eng (Priya Desai) 2026-03-10 11:10: Confirmed DHCP policy roll applied at 09:14; we accidentally set interface metric to 0 for ethernet profiles when we intended to set only route priority for guest vlan. Rolling back patch to branch-dhcp-02 now.

SRE (Daniel Kim) 2026-03-10 12:00: Observed conntrack resets on k8s nodes when source IPs mismatch. As a workaround we can add an iptables rule to ACCEPT related packets from the office subnet for a short window, but that weakens path validation. Prefer fixing DHCP/metrics.

Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-11 08:20: Documented user workaround: instruct users to unplug dock (fall back to wifi+vpn) or manually set network service order; shared KB draft: 'Docked laptop connection failures to internal APIs'.
Liam O'Connor 2026-03-13 09:45: Network rollback to DHCP patch completed on branch-dhcp-02 at 09:30. Asking QA to validate. Need to close after 48h of monitoring if no regressions.
resolution: Mitigation and rollback of DHCP metric change applied; temporary user workarounds provided; monitoring in place.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-10 13:10 - Network team rolled back DHCP metric change on branch-dhcp-02. New DHCP leases now advertise no default-gateway metric override.
2026-03-10 14:00 - SRE applied temporary iptables ACCEPT rule for office subnet to reduce impact while users recompiled leases (scheduled to be removed after verification).
2026-03-12 09:00 - Confirmed drop in reports; replica tests from docked hosts show symmetric routing restored.
Pending: remove temporary iptables rule on 2026-03-16 if no regressions observed.
follow_up_actions: Network: Add unit test / gating for DHCP option changes so metric overrides cannot be deployed without review (owner: Priya Desai).
Endpoint: Add endpoint-agent check that logs when a host has multiple default routes with identical metrics and report to /metrics (owner: Daniel Kim).
SRE: Schedule removal of temporary iptables rule 2026-03-16 unless rollover occurs (owner: Liam O'Connor).
Docs: Publish KB for users about docking best practices and how to reorder network services on macOS (owner: Ava Chen).
